change: Build a bounded TCP and epoll regression comparing write-mode registrations with and without EPOLLRDHUP after the send buffer fills.
evidence: Source inspection shows all connections retain RDHUP in both read and write epoll interests; the write path cannot act on RDHUP and returns on WouldBlock.
hypothesis: While writing to a stalled peer that has half-closed its send side, retaining level-triggered EPOLLRDHUP makes epoll wake repeatedly even when the socket is not writable.
next_action: Run a local socket regression before considering a single-change snapshot.
verdict: Unverified event-loop fairness risk; no retained behavior changed.
